headline: Partner at PwC - Specializing in Cybersecurity and Risk
about:
Kelly is a Principal in PwC’s Advisory Practice, based in Chicago, where she is a leader in the Firm’s Cybersecurity, Risk and Regulatory practice. With more than 25 years of experience in information security and cyber/tech risk management, she understands the cyber threat and risk landscape and how to help companies both manage that risk and enable their business. Leveraging that insight, Kelly specializes in helping organizations take a risk-based approach to asset protection and enterprise resiliency guiding executive teams on how to effectively focus the limited resources available on the initiatives that will bring the most value.  Kelly is often sought after to lead teams through the intricacies of enterprise transformation efforts involving the development and execution of strategies focused on modernizing the cyber function, the design and implementation of solutions, such as identity and access management and information protection, as well as, developing new target operating models that involve updated policies, standards, and re-engineered processes.

Working across a diverse portfolio of companies, Kelly also frequently advises Boards and executive teams on the ever changing regulatory landscape as it relates to cybersecurity.  She often works with her clients and leads teams to both assess compliance against cybersecurity regulations, such as FFIEC, NY DFS, NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), Cyber Risk Institute (CRI) Framework, NAIC cybersecurity principles, and OCC’s Heightened Standards, and assist with obtaining compliance.

Kelly is passionate about women in technology and cybersecurity and spends her time sponsoring and developing the next generation of female leaders both at PwC and in the market.  She helped found the initial Women in Technology inclusion group at PwC and participates with external groups such as Executive Women’s Forum (EWF) and Women in Cybersecurity (WiCyS).

experience.description:
With more than 25 years consulting in the cybersecurity and tech/cyber risk space, I have successfully led teams in delivering engagements across the broad spectrum of cybersecurity and risk for many global and regional Financial Institutions, primarily in the Banking and Capital Markets and Insurance sectors. Advises Boards of Directors and executive teams on how to become compliant with emerging laws/regulations focused on IT and Cybersecurity enhancements, as well as, designing and managing the program to help achieve compliance

Assists organizations in understanding the cyber threats posed to their environment and the vulnerabilities that exist to help the organization develop a cyber risk program and plan that allows the organization to be smarter about where their investment and efforts should go in enhancing their protection measures.

Leads teams, in response to a data breach, for example, that designs and develops data analytics solutions geared towards analyzing who has access to what system/data in an effort to minimize insider threat

projects.title: Computers and Computing Project
projects.description:
This project was to create a website for a company in need of a web developer.

When starting the project, I was able to design a web page for an imaginary company, or a real company that I would want to start up. The company had to be a not-for-profit, a service company, or a for-profit enterprise. I chose to build a website for a golf pro shop.

My job was to inform the world about my enterprise. I created a products and about page for the pro shop equipment and the employee information. All extra pages linked back to my home page which included information on the company's history.

I used XHTML to provide the structure and dictate the content of my pages. A CSS page was used to take care of all formatting, e.g., font selection, size and color, background color, positioning, etc.

projects.title: Informatics Group Project
projects.description:
This project's theme was based on this year's Microsoft Imagine Cup student competition. In the competition, students around the world are invited to use their skills, imagination, and passion to create a technology solution that addresses each year's theme.

This year’s theme: Imagine a World Where Technology Helps Solve the Toughest Problems.

In this team based assignment, I had the privilege of working with two other classmates. The goal of the project was to work together as a team and use technology to solve a problem of our choice from around the world.

In response to answering the projects main question, my teammates and I began by going through the process of defining our problem, researching, and creating a preliminary concept. We did not have to program or complete our final design, but did focus on creating a realistic solution. Our concept could have been anything from a website to a phone app or to a completely original information system, as long as it somehow connected to technology. The concept that my group and I ended up with was a video game, which teachers and students alike could use in the classroom. We believed that our concept addressed the issues of students not receiving enough hands on experience in the educational subject of science.This issue can be seen as a serious one because without any change students might experience huge gaps in their basic knowledge.

Once we had selected our group problem and mutually agreed on a concept, we began conducting research, gathering data, and developing a proposed video game based on our research and data. Ultimately, our group ended up developing a final website to display all of the information collected including our research, data, and solution. During the last week of class before winter break we presented the problem, and the proposed solution that included a realistic graphic of our prototype.

headline: Director Consulting Services at PwC
about:
I am an innovator and analytical problem solver at heart, and that is what drove me to pursue my education as a mechanical engineer. I obtained my BS and MS degree in Mechanical Engineering from Northwestern University as a 5 year fast track program offered by the university. Upon graduation I moved from my Midwestern roots in the northwestern suburbs of Chicago to start a new adventure in Houston with HP. In the last 6 years I have changed roles from a thermal engineer to a mechanical engineer specialist and witnessed various corporate reorganizations. Looking to further expand my horizons and in the interest of continued learning I enrolled in Fuqua's CCMBA program in July 2016 with a planned completion date of December 2017. The international exposure and team-based structure is what attracted me to the CCMBA program. 

My educational background in mechanical engineering is in design and manufacturing, with exposure to micro- and nano-technologies. Additionally, during my undergraduate and master's degree studies at NU I pursued a background in business and management, with an undergraduate minor in Business Institutions, and a graduate minor in Engineering Management. 

I began my career working as a summer intern for 5 years with Motorola Mobile Devices in both mechanical design and software development. With my experience in product development, design, and manufacturing, as well as being a lead engineer with responsibilities including schedule and cost optimization, I have striven to garner a career focused on using practical experience to drive business outcomes and deliver successful solutions to industry issues. 

Specialties: • Engineering: design and manufacturing, structural analysis, manufacturing, composite materials, MEMS/Nanotechnology
• Strategy: new product development, project management
• Computer Software: ProEngineer, Unigraphics NX, SolidWorks, Optistruct, Microsoft Office Suite
• Computer Programming: MATLAB, LabVIEW, Basic

Brad is a Partner in PwC’s greater Chicago practice.   In this role, he leads the audit process for public SEC registrants as well as privately held companies and he focusses on the fundamentals of high quality client service.  His areas of specialty include SEC reporting, SOX, business combinations, impairments, segment reporting, discontinued operations, consolidation and equity accounting. 

In addition, Brad serves as a Partner in PwC's Alliance with Workiva.  In this role, he helps client's maximize efficiencies in financial reporting and integrated risk management.  

Brad previously served in PwC's National Office, assisting Partners and Managers with accounting technical consultations and thought leadership. He is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA), licensed to practice in Illinois and Wisconsin and a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants.  Additionally Brad is a Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) and is Workiva Platform Certified.

about:
Over the past 20 years at PwC, I’ve had the privilege of guiding private equity and corporate clients through acquisition, divestiture and joint venture. Today, I’m proud to serve as the Deals Leader for PwC US and Mexico, building on my previous roles as Private Equity Leader and Deputy Deals Leader.  

I’ve had a particular focus on healthcare clients – from pharma, life sciences, medical devices, hospitals, to healthcare IT – supporting transactions ranging from $5M to $2B. I’m passionate about working with clients who are eager to push the edge of what’s possible in deals and value creation. 
 
Private equity has been a major focus throughout my career. I’ve worked closely with firms to help instill a cash culture, improve portfolio company performance, and deliver flawless transactions. At PwC, we bring an integrated approach that draws on our deep PE experience to anticipate challenges across the fund and portfolio lifecycle — making the complex world of private equity a little simpler and helping clients capture opportunity. 
 
Outside of work, I’m a proud husband and father of two children. Between work and children’s sporting events on the weekends, there isn’t much time left for personal hobbies! But as a family, we enjoy time together outside, hiking and soaking up all that the arts community in Chicago has to offer.  
 
You can learn more about me and PwC by clicking on the links in the ‘Featured’ section. If I can be of any assistance, please do not hesitate to reach out via LinkedIn.

publications.title: PwC Customer Loyalty Executive Survey 2023: Converting disconnects into loyalty opportunities
publications.description:
As companies continue to navigate market volatility, securing and expanding their relationships with their customers is perhaps more important than ever. Short-term pressures such as inflation and uncertain supply chains can push some leaders to reactively focus only on retention. But if you don’t understand how your customers make loyalty decisions throughout their journey with your brand, your business won’t be able to turn loyalty into real growth.

PwC surveyed more than 400 executives who are either responsible for or share influence regarding customer loyalty or retention decisions. We wanted to learn how well their companies are capitalizing on customer loyalty opportunities as they address current challenges. The PwC Customer Loyalty Executive Survey 2023 followed our May 2022 survey of more than 4,000 consumers in the United States. Taken together, the two surveys can help illustrate openings, moments and other pivotal points when you can increase customer engagement with your brands and improve the chances that they’ll not only stay but develop deeper bonds that turn loyalty into a growth engine.

publications.title: Creating loyalty in volatile times
publications.description:
Volatility in consumer behavior is at an all-time high. The COVID-19 pandemic fundamentally changed many needs and preferences. Inflation and a turbulent economy are influencing buying decisions. Technology creates unprecedented connectivity and access to goods and services. Consumers know more about where companies stand on environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues and expect businesses to share their beliefs. And let’s be honest: Consumers as a whole are more discerning than ever.

This all leaves companies wondering how they can better shape consumer demand and drive engagement with their brands. Unlocking what drives consumer loyalty has companies asking, “How do I attract and retain my customers?” Along with providing new insights from more than 4,000 consumers in the US, our PwC Customer Loyalty Survey 2022 reveals several opportunities for businesses to strengthen relationships, increase customer lifetime value and reduce the likelihood that they’ll leave.

publications.title: Bring your shades. The future looks bright
publications.description:
What will the future look like for travel after the abrupt standstill in early 2020? With vaccinations on the rise and infections on the decline in the US, a growing number of consumers are eager to get away. Many have the financial wherewithal, having been hunkered down at home for much of the past year, with fewer-than-usual opportunities to spend money. 

Despite this enthusiasm, many travel companies are struggling to visualize—and shape—the future of travel, recognizing that they need to acknowledge newly formed consumer expectations for trips to the mountains, the beach or the boardroom.

To understand the latest shifts in travel expectations, attitudes and behaviors—as well as the sustainability of those shifts—PwC surveyed more than 1,300 US consumers in April 2021 and compared the results to earlier surveys conducted in April and August of 2020. Most respondents to our latest survey told us they have at least one flight and/or an overnight stay planned for business or leisure within the next 12 months.

publications.title: Travelers on the move again
publications.description:
The travel industry is gradually moving again, but predicting travel demand is challenging in a rapidly changing environment. For now, self-quarantine measures required when traveling from high risk areas continue to keep most would-be travelers homebound. The good news: Once consumers take that first trip in this new environment, they are far more willing to travel again. However, a number of other factors — most of which stem from uncertainty — could continue to influence consumer travel behavior.

To stay current with evolving expectations, attitudes and behaviors about travel, PwC surveyed more than 1,000 consumers nationwide during the week of July 8, 2020, following an earlier survey conducted in April. All respondents had taken at least one flight or spent at least one night in a hotel in 2019.

publications.title: How to restore confidence in travel during an uncertain time
publications.description:
Safety is top of mind for consumers as they look beyond the current shelter-in-place mandates toward a recovery period when they can resume traveling. What else are they looking for beyond safety? What sources do they trust for information? What reassurances do they need when they travel?

To find out about expectations, attitudes and behaviors, PwC surveyed more than 1,000 consumers nationwide during the week of April 22. All respondents had taken at least one flight or spent at least one night in a hotel during 2019.

publications.title: Simplifying the Business - 2017 (New Ideas: Personalization)
publications.description:
The IATA Simplifying the Business (StB) program is a transformative driver of innovation through key projects and initiatives that aim to improve the passenger experience. Led by a group of innovation-focused airline representatives that are key transformers within their proper organizations, StB has become a cornerstone of innovation in IATA and across the industry

New Idea #3 - Personalization: 
Personalization has been at the forefront of travel sales, service, and delivery for over twenty years, but the technology needed to deliver personalization at scale is only just reaching
maturity. With strategic coordination between members of the travel ecosystem on the use of traveler data and clear standards for its management and application, the travel industry has the opportunity to deliver on the longstanding promise of a truly personalized travel experience.

publications.title: Digital operating models: How leading companies achieve results in the digital world
publications.description:
For this report, we identified a dozen global companies that have cracked the digital code—turning high-level talk about digital strategy into meaningful, high-quality, operational action across the enterprise in a consistent, fast, and predictable way. These companies are globally located and span major industry sectors, including consumer goods, travel and hospitality, financial services,
healthcare, and retail. Our goal was to learn from these digital exemplars and identify the leading 
 practices of a digital operating model.

Prior to joining the Philadelphia M&A Tax practice, Shawn was a director in the Washington National Tax Services ("WNTS") M&A Tax Practice within PwC. WNTS is the technical core of PwC's tax practice. The WNTS M&A Tax practice is a premier, highly experienced team, including former senior Congressional, Treasury, and IRS officials, that assists companies in staying up to date on the latest legislative, regulatory, and judicial matters, and helps companies navigate the ever-changing tax landscape. The PwC WNTS M&A Tax team delivers innovative tax advice on some of the largest and most complex corporate transactions. 

Shawn's practice focuses advising on tax-free reorganizations, spin-offs and similar transactions, the cross-border implications of corporate transactions, redemption transactions, global restructurings, and taxable acquisitions. In addition, Shawn's expertise focuses on the preservation of tax attributes (including U.S. federal net operating losses). Shawn has performed numerous Section 382 studies on both public and privately held corporations throughout many different industries. 

Shawn obtained his Master of Laws in Taxation from the University of Miami School of Law, his Juris Doctor from Duquesne University School of Law, and his Bachelor of Arts from the Pennsylvania State University. Shawn is also licensed to practice law in the state of Pennsylvania.

publications.title: Four Components to Foundational Data
publications.description: GenAI, data science and a broad appetite for analytics has been out of the shadows for a while now, and carriers now have to find ways to democratize their data.  But there’s a big problem. Data remains virtually unusable in layer upon layer of systems, sprawling and disconnected. There is no enterprise data model.  The leap from a complex, ad hoc, ungoverned world to one of order and trust is hard for many carriers to fathom. Ultimately, they have to decide that they can’t endure the pain of being an invertebrate anymore and commit to having a backbone – an enterprise data backbone

publications.title: Out with the many: Redesigning distributor compensation as a shared service
publications.description:
Cutting costs, tapping transparency

Insurance carriers today are wondering: How can they lower fixed costs? Meanwhile, their distribution partners are looking for greater transparency and ease of doing business. We maintain that by addressing fragmented legacy operating environments, carriers can address both of these challenges.

The typical multi-line insurance carrier today maintains many different systems to pay compensation to distribution partners, usually as a result of M&A activity without subsequent consolidation. As a result, when partners deal with multiple business units across the company, their experience is inconsistent and disjointed. These partners are now demanding an improved experience, and arguably the most important touchpoint between a carrier and its partners is compensation.

publications.title: BPO for the Life & Annuity market
publications.description:
Life and annuity insurers are focusing on three areas to drive growth: distribution, product and brand. Growth is hard enough in today’s market, but it’s even harder when your back office holds you back, both in terms of fixed costs and limited capabilities. Accordingly, achieving operational efficiency is table stakes for life & annuity insurers competing in an extended soft market.  

Fortunately, given recent advances in technology and expansion of provider capabilities, business process outsourcing (BPO) has become a feasible way to reduce costs and increase efficiencies. Based on what we’ve seen in the market, we think BPO providers are ready to move from their traditional role as vendors to true business partner.  With scale, advanced technology,
and money to invest, the best of them offer great opportunity for insurers to significantly lower costs and benefit from complementary services over the long term.

publications.title: What's the Problem with 'best practices'?
publications.description:
In our recent non-scientific sampling of top U.S and Global personal lines and commercial lines executives, representing the entire gamut of functional areas, we asked – what’s the problem with best practices? We listened to their struggles and heard some success stories as well. 
Risk Manager’s strive toward best practices, and it’s a long hard road.

publications.title: Simplicity is the Ultimate Sophistication: How Life Insurers Can Streamline Incentive Compensation for their Producers
publications.description:
The complex web of compensation schedules that has evolved over time is reaching a critical mass. The demand for simplicity and transparency in producer compensation is arising from demographic, industry, and regulatory factors.

We have observed carriers struggling with a proliferation of schedules and incentives that are not aligned with strategy, while leading carriers are establishing the flexibility to craft compensation that aligns with corporate goals. Once this flexibility is established, carriers are better able to distinguish themselves from competitors in agents’ eyes. In our view, carriers should reduce the overall number of plans offered before replacing the underlying systems supporting incentive compensation. Without simplification before system transformation, carriers will re-platform legacy problems and miss out on many possible benefits.

headline: Manager, Healthcare Provider Transformation, PwC
about: I am a former critical care RN and have worked in a variety of healthcare settings and roles. I currently act as a consultant to healthcare organizations that wish to improve operational efficiency via process improvement and technological innovation. I've helped organizations identify and define strategic goals, increase margins through increased reimbursement and cost takeout, and standardize processes across functional units. I enjoy finding innovative solutions to problems that are backed by data and science, especially using technological tools. The intersection of clinical care, technology, and business is where I impact the healthcare industry.

experience.description: As a Manager in healthcare transformation efforts focused on strategic planning, pharmacy optimization, reimbursement strategies, and operational automation. I managed the development of a five-year strategic plan for a pediatric and family support nonprofit, integrating demand projections, hospital partnerships, and funding innovation strategies to optimize capacity, referral networks, and reimbursement pathways. I guided a multi-workstream transformation effort that combined occupancy modeling, Medicaid/waiver policy analysis, and family experience insights to create a decision framework supporting efficiency, diversified revenue streams, and long-term impact. I facilitated end-to-end strategic planning by aligning stakeholder input, market analysis, and organizational priorities into a multi-year roadmap with defined goals, metrics, and decision points. I spearheaded pharmacy optimization across multiple facilities by consolidating formularies, aligning rebate submissions across 10+ EMRs, and validating wholesaler pricing, generating $6.5M in benefit. I partnered with pharmacy leaders and IT teams to standardize IVIG dosing using evidence-based guidelines and compliance tracking, securing system-wide adoption. I streamlined CMS Occupational Mix Survey reporting for 100+ facilities by creating Python automations and machine learning models to classify nursing labor, reducing manual work, accelerating project delivery, and generating $5.9M in firm revenue. I engineered automation solutions to eliminate repetitive reporting tasks, standardize processes, and improve data reliability. I led cross-functional teams through complex integrations, aligning clinical, IT, and finance stakeholders on pharmacy workflows and reimbursement. I also developed dashboards and sustainability models to support continuous process improvement and post-deployment tracking.
skills: Interact with All Levels Of Management

experience.description: As a Senior Associate, I specialized in workforce optimization, perioperative process redesign, and revenue recovery across multi-site health systems. I designed and standardized staffing matrixes, productivity models, and OR scheduling systems to streamline nursing workflows, optimize workforce utilization, and align staffing with patient demand. I developed processes for perioperative preference card maintenance, procedure table updates, OR system optimization, and quality metric capture, improving standardization and data consistency. I co-led the design, build, testing, and go-live of a physician office scheduling platform integrated within a streamlined OR information system, reducing redundant processes and improving scheduling efficiency. I optimized OR supply chain par levels by benchmarking against national standards and historical utilization, reducing and redistributing unused product, saving ~$500K annually. I implemented 340B programs by overcoming data integration and compliance challenges, standardizing configurations, and conducting internal audits, resulting in $1M+ in facility savings. I automated and standardized Medicare bad debt and uncompensated care documentation using low-code solutions, producing defensible audit packets and enabling millions in additional reimbursement per provider. I directed care reporting workstreams by validating and integrating multi-system data, resolving inconsistencies with automation, and incorporating auditor feedback to enhance submission quality and audit readiness. I also managed distributed analytics and research teams across time zones using structured handoffs, standardized templates, and automation tools, ensuring timely, audit-ready Medicare deliverables that consistently met client expectations.
skills: Interact with All Levels Of Management

experience.description: In my role as an Experienced Associate, I focused on hospital operations optimization, clinical workflow redesign, and digital automation. I reduced patient length of stay (LOS) by aligning care management with GMLOS benchmarks through standardized interdisciplinary rounds, predictive discharge planning, and regression modeling of order sets. I facilitated executive design sessions to co-develop future-state workflows customized to organizational needs, reducing LOS by 5–15% in complex cases and improving navigation across departments. I standardized workflows across an 11-hospital system, overcoming governance and technology challenges by implementing centralized reporting, embedding leadership, tailoring site-level deployments, and automating processes. I leveraged automation to extract EMR data using RPA-driven bots in environments lacking direct database connectivity, ensuring continued access to essential clinical insights. I also automated data cleansing and analysis pipelines to accelerate reporting, reduce errors, and improve delivery of actionable insights. As part of PwC’s inaugural Digital Accelerators program, I pioneered healthcare-centered automation strategies, introducing bots, predictive modeling, and workflow automation into core delivery models. This experience allowed me to merge clinical knowledge with advanced technology to redesign care delivery, increase efficiency, and enhance financial and operational outcomes across client systems.

about:
Nick Grott: Financial Services and Cyber Risk Specialist

Nick Grott is an accomplished professional based in Chicago, with a solid foundation in finance and informatics from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. His academic background has provided him with the analytical and technical skills necessary for a career in financial services and consulting.

Nick began his professional journey as a Business Analyst Intern at the Federal Reserve Bank, where he gained critical insights into financial regulation and policy analysis. He then further developed his expertise with a dual-role internship in Finance and Accounting at Aon, focusing on financial analysis, accounting procedures, and internal controls.

Currently, Nick is a Senior Associate at PwC, where he has spent the past two years as a Cyber Risk Consultant in the financial services sector. His responsibilities include issue validation, control testing, and internal audit functions, with a strong emphasis on addressing confidential supervisory findings. Nick is proficient in utilizing tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, Forms, SharePoint, as well as a variety of applications used by financial institutions. Additionally, he has strong skills in presenting to both internal and external client leadership.

Nick is committed to collaborative work that drives meaningful impact within financial institutions. He is dedicated to understanding the larger purpose of his work and how it fits into the financial regulatory landscape. Consulting allows him to continuously acquire new skills and engage with professionals nationwide, enriching his expertise in the financial domain.

about:
As an AWS Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, I thrive on solving complex challenges and empowering businesses to fully harness the potential of cloud technology. With a proven track record in designing, deploying, and managing scalable, high-availability systems on AWS, I specialize in delivering impactful, tailored solutions that align with diverse business goals.

I have played a pivotal role in architecting robust AWS infrastructures by configuring VPCs, subnets, route tables, and internet gateways to build secure and efficient network architectures. Utilizing services like Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, EC2, RDS, and S3, I ensure optimal performance, high availability, and cost efficiency for my clients.

Security and compliance are at the heart of my work. I implement rigorous access controls using IAM policies, security groups, and NACLs, while leveraging tools such as Amazon CloudWatch and AWS CloudTrail to maintain visibility and integrity across systems.

I’m deeply passionate about automation and DevOps practices. I excel in building and managing CI/CD pipelines using tools like GitHub, Jenkins, SonarQube, Prometheus, and Nexus, ensuring seamless code integration, thorough quality assurance, and efficient deployment processes.
Additionally, I bring extensive expertise in Kubernetes (EKS), including provisioning EKS clusters with self-managed nodes and managing deployments to support scalable, resilient, and containerized applications.

Also, I am experienced in Vendor Security Assessment, Network Design, and Vulnerability Management and I possess in-depth knowledge of standards and frameworks including ISO 27001/27002, NIST, CIS, CCM, PCI DSS, GDPR, etc. My skills in security privacy controls and assessments are complemented by a proven track record of delivering exceptional risk management support. Resilient, data-driven, self-motivated, and passionate about continuous learning and development, I am committed to advancing cybersecurity practices and enhancing organizational security. By combining technical excellence with a forward-thinking approach, I enable businesses to innovate, scale, and achieve their goals with cutting-edge cloud solutions.

about:
I am a Chicago based Deals Partner focused on helping clients identify and execute on the deals that accelerate their business strategy and generate value now and into the future.  I advise clients on the accounting and financial reporting complexity that arises throughout the deal cycle for acquisitions, carve-out divestitures and spin-off transactions as well as capital markets activities including IPOs and high yield debt offerings.  

I have over twenty-eight years of experience providing both core attestation and accounting advisory services to clients in a variety of industries with a focus on industrial products, pharma life sciences and retail and consumer markets.

Prior to 2006, I was a part of PwC’s core assurance team serving as the lead manager on key audit clients across multiple industry sectors and was integrally involved in the initial and go forward compliance efforts of my clients with the requirements of the Sarbanes-Oxley legislation.

Developed an interactive tool that connects cancer patients to potential drugs and clinical trial treatment options based on patient-specific gene mutation, cancer type, and cancer stage for several prevalent cancer diagnoses in the US. Cleaned and transformed over 1 million patient records in a custom ETL pipeline, collected using Web-APIs with Python from different sources. Developed an interactive dashboard where patients find actively recruiting clinical trials based on their individual diagnosis type and stage.

I help create great user experiences through sophisticated strategy and inclusive design.

I spent my collegiate years studying at Indiana University where I studied marketing and international business along with Spanish. I continued on there to study information systems through the MSIS program, which led me to my opportunity at PwC. 

Before choosing PwC, I was stuck between two pathways that would dictate the start of my career. One followed family traditions and the other was a relatively new path, unknown to my family and in a new state. I chose the less familiar path and moved to Chicago to begin my career at PwC in the Experience Center.

While I chose to move back to Indianapolis in the midst of the pandemic, my career at PwC has remained strong and passionate.

headline: Consultant, intelligence, thought leadership
about:
Trine Tsouderos is a communications and intelligence executive with expansive experience producing forward-looking analysis and insights, particularly for US health industries. In 2023, Tsouderos was Senior Vice President of Intelligence at Vizient and Sg2. For nearly a decade, Tsouderos worked for Health Research Institute, PwC's independent healthcare think tank. Tsouderos was one of the founders and original co-hosts of PwC's healthcare podcast, Next in Health, which continues to be produced to this day.

A former journalist, Tsouderos has 17 years of newsroom experience. She was a science and medical reporter at the Chicago Tribune, winning state and national awards for her work. Her work has been cited in books and scientific papers. Tsouderos lives outside Chicago with her husband, two children, and a Bernese Mountain Dog.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

experience.description: I led the vision and research agenda for Vizient and Sg2, including a team of 50 subject matter experts.

As a director in PwC's consulting solutions services and a member of the firm's storied and specialized vaccine/ID team, dubbed the "Vaccine Tiger Team", Trine worked with pharmaceutical and life sciences companies on COVID-19, influenza and other vaccines, mRNA technology, infectious disease (ID) forecasting and ID-related therapeutics. PwC's vaccine team specializes in vaccines, mRNA, mAbs, disease forecasting and US and global policy revolving around pandemics and ID. The team aids companies with commercial drug launches, policy landscape assessments, strategy and other projects.

Trine Tsouderos led PwC's Business Insights, Sectors team, which produces forward-looking thought leadership on industries including healthcare, technology, media, telecommunications, banking and capital markets, asset wealth management, private equity, energy, utilities, mining, industrial and consumer products and more. The team's goal is to offer executives vision into what's coming next in their industries and to help them pilot their organizations through the many changes underway in many areas of the domestic and global economy.

Trine also was co-host of PwC's healthcare podcast, Next in Health, with PwC Strategy& principal Igor Belokrinitsky.

publications.title: Health reform 2.0 A guide to developing resilience amid an uncertain future for the Affordable Care Act
Surviving seismic change: Winning a piece of the $5 trillion US health ecosystem
publications.description: Where is the US health industry heading over the next 10 years? Which forces are reshaping the industry, how fast are they moving and how will they impact health organizations, both new and established? How has care changed – or not changed – for American health consumers?

publications.title: The pharmacy of the future: Hub of personalized health
publications.description: Retail pharmacies face shrinking margins in their core business and tougher competition in a shifting health industry. Yet these companies have the opportunity to redefine themselves as central players – and critical partners – in the New Health Economy.To paint a portrait of the present and future of retail pharmacies, PwC’s Health Research Institute (HRI) interviewed executives from Fortune 50 drugstore companies, big box retailers, supermarket chains, startups, prescription benefit managers and others. What emerged is a picture of an industry at a crossroads, but with three strategic opportunities: Become a health hub for consumers, deliver new value to traditional partners and new entrants and master the “last mile” to meet consumers where they are both virtually and physically.

publications.title: The coming plug-and-play health ecosystem
publications.description:
The health industry has long been a closed and highly-siloed system.
But powerful global forces are transforming the industry into a
nimble, innovative and modular ecosystem serving the consumer,
with profound implications for players new and traditional.

publications.title: Money matters: Payment and billing for a New Health Economy
publications.description: The nation's healthcare billing and payment system is an artifact of an earlier age. Much can be done to improve the system in the short term, but in the long term, structural change is needed. In this report, HRI diagnoses the billing and payment system, and prescribes short- and long-term solutions.

publications.title: The Future of Health Is More, Better, Cheaper
publications.description: Within a decade, the health business will look and feel like other consumer-oriented, technology-enabled industries. Soon, it will have its own Amazon.com-style, iconic, new economy brands—companies that can give consumers an easy way to access information, doctors, and treatments; provide them with a variety of services and products for a variety of prices; and centralize their care through user-friendly interfaces. And thanks to this growing trend, there are plenty of new entrants into the market who would like nothing better than to upend the old model of care and empower consumers, while taking some of the industry’s US$2.9 trillion market share for themselves.

publications.title: Top health industry issues of 2015
publications.description: Every year, PwC's Health Research Institute names the top issues that will shape the US healthcare industry in the coming year. This year, DIY healthcare, a drive for partnerships and the tension between convenience and security for health data are among the top issues. Read more in HRI's annual report.

publications.title: Health wearables: Early days
publications.description: While the smartphone remains Americans’ device of choice, the tech world is creating a future of wearable technology that promises to entertain consumers, save them money and help them live healthier lives. Technology companies’ interests in health and wellness have sparked the creation of a myriad of wearable devices, from fitness bands that monitor activity and sleep patterns   to flexible patches that can detect body temperature, respiration rate, hydration level, blood pressure and more.

publications.title: Healthcare's new entrants:  Who will be the industry's Amazon.com
publications.description: The health sector’s center of gravity is shifting toward consumers and new tech-savvy players are moving fast to capitalize on the change. These new entrants are poised to shake up the industry, drawing billions of dollars in revenue from traditional healthcare organizations while building lucrative new markets in the burgeoning New Health Economy.

projects.title: Project Run With It
projects.description:
Project Run With It (PRWI) furthers the community service component of Beta Alpha Psi and provides members/candidates with an opportunity to engage in a real-world consulting project.

As Beta Alpha Psi celebrates its 100th year anniversary, PRWI begins its 12th year with exciting news! There has been such a positive response from student participants and the nonprofit organizations served that we have decided to expand the competition and allow more students the opportunity to be involved. PRWI 2019 will involve up to 96 BAP student representatives working together during the annual meeting to develop solutions to real-life business problems of actual not-for-profit (NFP) organizations located in the greater Chicago, IL area. Working in teams of four, students will have the equivalent of one and half working days to develop a formal presentation showcasing their solution to the business issues presented by the NFPs in their request for proposal for consulting services. Prior to the annual meeting, the NFP organizations will provide background information to all participating students and will be on site Wednesday evening to answer students' questions.

Sheri’s background includes experience in providing holistic tailored tax services to her clients including gifting, trusts, private foundations, and investment partnerships.

Sheri serves a variety of clients including high net worth individuals, business owners, family offices, senior level executives, and owners of private equity & hedge fund firms to minimize both income taxes and wealth transfer taxes.  Although most of her clients are generally rooted in the Midwest, Sheri serves clients across the entire US and abroad.

In 1998, Sheri earned a Bachelor of Science degree from University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, majoring in Accountancy.  She became a Certified Public Accountant in 1999.  Then in 2003, she completed the Master of Science in Taxation curriculum at DePaul University in Chicago.

headline: Private, Assurance Services, Partner at PwC US
about:
Lisa’s perseverance and tenacity are evident in what she sets out to accomplishment – whether it is completing the Breast Cancer 3 day walk despite serious physical injuries to both feet or taking companies public, clients can expect that she is fully engaged and committed to seeing things through.    Considered a go-to for her technical knowledge, her impact is built on the power of deep, connected relationships.  Compelled to help others, she has a passion for giving and seeing them succeed.  Others know that through her calm, collaborative and approachable nature, she is committed to her clients and teams having their best interests at heart.  Lisa is proud to be an Audit partner with PwC, leveraging thought leadership and leading clients through tough technical issues by listening, understanding their ultimate goals and quickly guiding them to resolution.

Lisa inspires by example as a leader and working mother of a child with disabilities.  Her strong Atlanta roots make her proud to be a home-grown female public company audit partner.  In addition to being a champion for her clients and team, as the mother of a child with differing abilities, she is an advocate for raising awareness of the power of diverse abilities in the workplace.   She has most recently been featured in Working Mother’s Magazine, regarding work-life balance, and the Chicago Tribune, discussing the PwC Disability Caregivers Network in the US, which she leads. She loves helping others who suddenly find themselves on this tough road of being a working parent of a child with special needs.  Lisa is also a member and past President of the Board of Directors for CURE Childhood Cancer and aims to help cure childhood cancer in her lifetime.  

Lisa enjoys meeting and connecting with new people in the community.

about:
Vanessa is a Partner at PwC with leadership responsibilities across market, solutions and service teams. With almost 15 years' experience at PwC, she has held various leadership roles, including leading service teams for many of PwC's largest clients, with a focus on the technology, media and telecommunications (TMT) and private equity (PE) sectors. 

Office Managing Partner: Vanessa is the Office Managing Partner for PwC's NY office. As the face of the firm to the local community and businesses, she is passionate about driving market-driven corporate responsibility initiatives and delivering value to clients. She believes in providing pragmatic solutions balanced with creative flexibility to save clients time and money. She is equally passionate about all aspects of firm-wide activities, including people, community and workplace management.

Deals and Private Equity: In her role as Cyber Risk and Reg's (CRR) Deals Solution Lead and PE CRR Platform Lead, Vanessa ensures that clients receive expert guidance and advice to maximise deal value and reduce transaction risk. By focusing on the technology and digital aspects of a transaction, Vanessa advances her clients' objectives as they undertake complex, global integrations, divestitures, separations and joint ventures. Her clients value approaches that accelerate risk identification and mitigation strategies to achieve desired deal synergies and increase shareholder value.

Transformation, XaaS, Analytics & Automation: Vanessa has also worked with clients undergoing complex business transformations, advising them on the cross-functional implications specifically related to their business processes, systems and controls. Vanessa has also led the analysis of data at scale, including big data analysis, data validation and visual analytics. She also leads system implementations, particularly for solutions that support revenue growth through subscription and consumption business models and the new leasing standard. 

In addition, Vanessa has extensive and broad assurance experience in areas such as SEC, technical accounting, financial and operational controls, internal audit and compliance. She is a national speaker at various forums. She is a Certified Public Accountant in NY and a Fellow of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. She is extremely passionate about making a difference in the community and serves on several non-profit boards and is a committed supporter of issues such as mental health, education and poverty/equality for all.
